_metadata.purpose: Descriptions of compliance_answers fields that article modules read and that were missing from the answers template (template-gap task, 2026-10-04). Merged into core/context.py _FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS and returned by cl_analyze_project as compliance_answers_field_descriptions.
_metadata.verification: Drafted by Claude; every text verified by o3 against Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 before release. The art48 texts, art49.claims_art6_3_exception and art52.is_gpai_with_systemic_risk were reviewed by o3 on 2026-10-12 (review items J16 and J17); the texts the review reworded or added are stored in its wording.
_metadata.placeholders: {chapter_iii_annex_iii} / {chapter_iii_annex_i}: Art. 113 Chapter III dates, filled from data/application_dates.json at load (core/context.py); o3 verified the texts with the dates of 2026-10-04 (2 December 2027 / 2 August 2028).

art4.literacy_description: Free text: the AI literacy measures you found (training material, onboarding, internal guidance) that the provider or deployer takes to support the AI literacy of its staff and other persons dealing with the operation and use of AI systems on its behalf (Art. 4(1)). Leave empty if there is nothing to report.

art6.annex_iii_categories: List of the Annex III points the intended purpose falls under, using the Annex III identifier and including a letter where one exists, e.g. ["1(a)", "2", "4(a)", "5(b)"]; [] if none. A listed point makes the system potentially high-risk under Art. 6(2).
art6.annex_i_product_type: Free text: for Art. 6(1), identify the product of which the AI system is intended to be a safety component, or the product that the AI system itself constitutes, and the Union harmonisation legislation listed in Annex I that covers that product; also state whether the AI system qualifies as a safety component taking Art. 6(1a) and (1b) into account, and whether the product is required under that legislation to undergo a third-party conformity assessment for placing on the market or putting into service, taking Art. 6(1c) into account. Leave empty if Art. 6(1) is not relevant or you cannot determine these facts from the project.
art6.has_risk_classification_doc: true if, for an AI system referred to in Annex III that the provider considers not to be high-risk under Art. 6(3), the project shows that the provider documented that assessment before the system was placed on the market or put into service; false if the provider relies on Art. 6(3) but no such pre-market or pre-service documentation is present; null if you cannot determine it from the project or the provider does not rely on Art. 6(3).
art6.reasoning: Free text: your reasoning for the risk classification of the system under Art. 6 (Annex I, Annex III, and the Art. 6(3) derogation where relied on). Leave empty if there is nothing to report.

art10.uses_model_training: true if the high-risk AI system is developed using techniques involving the training of AI models with data; false if it is developed without techniques involving the training of AI models, in which case Art. 10(2), (3) and (4) and Art. 4a(1) apply only to the testing data sets (Art. 10(6)); null if you cannot determine it from the project.

art12.logging_description: Free text: how the system automatically records events (logs) over its lifetime (Art. 12(1)) — the logging library, what is recorded and where it is stored. Leave empty if there is nothing to report.
art12.retention_days: Number: the retention period, in days, configured or otherwise evidenced for the logs referred to in Art. 12(1) that are automatically generated by the high-risk AI system and are under the provider's control; null if no such retention period is configured or evidenced, or you cannot determine it. Art. 19(1) requires those logs to be kept for a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in the applicable Union or national law, in particular Union law on the protection of personal data.
art12.retention_evidence: Free text: where the retention period for the automatically generated logs referred to in Art. 12(1), to the extent those logs are under the provider's control, is configured or otherwise documented (file, setting, policy). Leave empty if there is nothing to report.

art16.has_documentation_kept: true if the provider keeps the documentation referred to in Art. 18 (technical documentation, quality management system documentation, documentation of changes approved by notified bodies, decisions of notified bodies, EU declaration of conformity) for the period set there (Art. 16(d)); false if it does not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art16.has_log_retention: true if the provider keeps the logs automatically generated by its high-risk AI systems, to the extent they are under its control, as referred to in Art. 19 (Art. 16(e)); false if it does not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art16.has_conformity_assessment: true if the high-risk AI system has undergone the relevant conformity assessment procedure referred to in Art. 43 before it is placed on the market or put into service; false if it has been placed on the market or put into service without having undergone that procedure; null if you cannot determine it from the project or the system has not yet reached the point at which the procedure must have been completed.
art16.has_eu_declaration: true if the provider has drawn up an EU declaration of conformity in accordance with Art. 47 for the high-risk AI system (Art. 16(g)); false if it has not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art16.has_ce_marking: true if the CE marking is affixed to the high-risk AI system or, where that is not possible, on its packaging or accompanying documentation, in accordance with Art. 48 (Art. 16(h)); false if it is not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art16.has_registration: true if the provider complies with the registration obligations referred to in Art. 49(1) (registration in the EU database) for the high-risk AI system (Art. 16(i)); false if it does not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art16.has_corrective_actions_process: true if the project documents a process under which, when the provider considers or has reason to consider that a high-risk AI system it placed on the market or put into service is not in conformity with the Regulation, it immediately takes the necessary corrective actions and provides the information required by Art. 20, including the further investigation and authority information required where the system presents a risk within the meaning of Art. 79(1); false if no such process is present; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art16.has_conformity_evidence: true if the provider can demonstrate, upon a reasoned request of a national competent authority, the conformity of the high-risk AI system with the requirements of Chapter III, Section 2 (Art. 16(k)) — e.g. the technical documentation and test records are maintained and retrievable; false if it cannot; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art16.has_accessibility_compliance: true if the high-risk AI system complies with accessibility requirements in accordance with Directives (EU) 2016/2102 and (EU) 2019/882 (Art. 16(l)); false if it does not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.

art18.retention_policy_evidence: Free text: where the project shows that the provider keeps the documentation listed in Art. 18(1) at the disposal of the national competent authorities for a period ending 10 years after the high-risk AI system has been placed on the market or put into service (for example, an archive policy, retention configuration or repository evidence). Leave empty if there is nothing to report.

art19.retention_days: Number: the retention period, in days, configured or otherwise evidenced for the logs referred to in Art. 12(1) that are automatically generated by the high-risk AI system and are under the provider's control; null if no such period is configured or evidenced, or you cannot determine it. Art. 19(1) requires a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in the applicable Union or national law, in particular Union law on the protection of personal data.
art19.retention_evidence: Free text: where the retention period for logs automatically generated by the high-risk AI system, to the extent those logs are under the provider's control, is configured or otherwise documented (file, setting, policy). Leave empty if there is nothing to report.

art22.has_mandate_authority_contact: true if the written mandate of the authorised representative empowers it to be addressed, in addition to or instead of the provider, by the competent authorities on all issues related to ensuring compliance with the Regulation (Art. 22(3)); false if it does not; null if you cannot determine it from the project or no authorised representative is appointed.

art25.has_third_party_written_agreement: true if, where Art. 25(4) applies, the provider of the high-risk AI system and the third party supplying an AI system, AI model, tools, services, components or processes used or integrated in it have a written agreement specifying the necessary information, capabilities, technical access and other assistance based on the generally acknowledged state of the art so that the provider can fully comply with the Regulation; false if Art. 25(4) applies but no such written agreement exists; null if you cannot determine it from the project, there is no such third party, or the third party falls within the Art. 25(4) exception for tools, services, processes or components made accessible to the public under a free and open-source licence, other than general-purpose AI models.
art25.has_open_source_exception: true if the relevant third party makes tools, services, processes or components accessible to the public under a free and open-source licence and the supplied item is not a general-purpose AI model, so that the written-agreement obligation in Art. 25(4) does not apply to that supply; false if those conditions are not met; null if you cannot determine it from the project.

art26.has_log_retention: true if the deployer keeps the logs automatically generated by the high-risk AI system, to the extent such logs are under its control, for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, of at least six months, unless applicable Union or national law provides otherwise (Art. 26(6)); false if it does not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art26.retention_days: Number: the retention period, in days, configured or otherwise evidenced for logs automatically generated by the high-risk AI system to the extent those logs are under the deployer's control; null if no such period is configured or evidenced, or you cannot determine it. Art. 26(6) requires a period appropriate to the intended purpose of the high-risk AI system, of at least six months, unless provided otherwise in applicable Union or national law, in particular Union law on the protection of personal data.
art26.retention_evidence: Free text: where the retention period for logs automatically generated by the high-risk AI system, to the extent those logs are under the deployer's control, is configured or otherwise documented (file, setting, policy). Leave empty if there is nothing to report.
art26.has_affected_persons_notification: true if, without prejudice to Art. 50, the deployer of a high-risk AI system referred to in Annex III that makes decisions or assists in making decisions related to natural persons informs those natural persons that they are subject to the use of the high-risk AI system (Art. 26(11)); false if it does not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.

art48.has_ce_marking: true if the CE marking is affixed to the high-risk AI system visibly, legibly and indelibly or, where that is not possible or not warranted on account of the nature of the high-risk AI system, to its packaging or its accompanying documentation, as appropriate (Art. 48(3)); false if it is not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art48.has_digital_ce_marking: true if a digital CE marking is used for the high-risk AI system and can easily be accessed via the interface from which the system is accessed or via an easily accessible machine-readable code or other electronic means (Art. 48(2)); false if no digital CE marking is used or it cannot easily be accessed in one of these ways; null if you cannot determine it from the project or the system is not provided digitally.
art48.has_notified_body_number: true if the CE marking is followed by the identification number of the notified body responsible for the conformity assessment procedure set out in Art. 43 (Art. 48(4), first sentence); false if it is not; null if you cannot determine it from the project or no notified body is involved.
art48.has_notified_body_number_in_promotion: true if every identified promotional material that mentions that the high-risk AI system fulfils the requirements for CE marking also indicates the notified body's identification number; false if at least one such item omits it; null if compliance cannot be determined
art48.follows_general_ce_marking_principles: true if the evidence establishes that the CE marking is subject to the general principles in Article 30 of Regulation (EC) No 765/2008; false if the evidence establishes a breach; null if this cannot be determined
art48.notified_body_number_affixed_by_permitte: true if the notified-body identification number was affixed by the notified body itself or, under its instructions, by the provider or the provider's authorised representative; false if the evidence establishes that it was affixed outside those permitted cases; null if this cannot be determined
art48.ce_marking_indicates_other_union_law_com: true if, where the system is subject to other Union law also requiring CE marking, the CE marking indicates that the high-risk AI system also fulfils the requirements of that other law; false if it does not; null if this cannot be determined
art48.is_provided_digitally: true if the high-risk AI system is provided digitally, in which case Art. 48(2) requires a digital CE marking; false if it is not provided digitally; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art48.has_notified_body_assessment: true if a notified body is responsible for the conformity assessment procedure set out in Art. 43 for the high-risk AI system, in which case Art. 48(4) requires its identification number after the CE marking; false if the procedure involves no notified body (e.g. the conformity assessment procedure based on internal control referred to in Annex VI); null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art48.is_subject_to_other_ce_marking_law: true if the high-risk AI system is subject to other Union law which also provides for the affixing of the CE marking, in which case the CE marking indicates that the system also fulfils the requirements of that other law (Art. 48(5)); false if it is not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art48.has_ce_marking_promotional_material: true if the project contains promotional material which mentions that the high-risk AI system fulfils the requirements for CE marking; false if the project establishes that no such promotional material exists; null if this cannot be determined

art49.claims_art6_3_exception: true if the provider considers that the AI system, although referred to in Annex III, is not high-risk under Article 6(3), because it does not pose a significant risk of harm to the health, safety or fundamental rights of natural persons, at least one condition in Article 6(3)(a)–(d) is fulfilled, and it does not perform profiling of natural persons, and the provider relies on that assessment; false if no such assessment is relied on; null if this cannot be determined from the project

art51.training_compute_flops: Number: the cumulative amount of computation used for training the general-purpose AI model, measured in floating point operations (e.g. 1e25); null if you cannot determine it. A model is presumed to have high-impact capabilities when this amount is greater than 10^25 (Art. 51(2)).
art51.has_systemic_risk_assessment: true if the project establishes that the general-purpose AI model meets at least one condition in Art. 51(1): it has high-impact capabilities evaluated on the basis of appropriate technical tools and methodologies, including indicators and benchmarks, or the Commission has decided that it has capabilities or an impact equivalent to such high-impact capabilities having regard to Annex XIII; false if the project establishes that neither condition is met; null if you cannot determine it. For Art. 51(1)(a), take into account the Art. 51(2) presumption where cumulative training computation is greater than 10^25 floating point operations.
art51.has_commission_designation: true if the Commission has decided that the general-purpose AI model has capabilities or an impact equivalent to high-impact capabilities, having regard to the criteria in Annex XIII (Art. 51(1)(b)); false if not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art51.reasoning: Free text: your reasoning for whether the general-purpose AI model is a model with systemic risk under Art. 51 (training compute, capabilities, Commission decision). Leave empty if there is nothing to report.

art52.notification_evidence: Free text: where the Art. 52(1) notification to the Commission is documented, including evidence that it was made without delay and in any event within two weeks after the Art. 51(1)(a) condition was met or it became known that it would be met, and that it included the information necessary to demonstrate that the condition was met. Leave empty if there is nothing to report.
art52.is_gpai_with_systemic_risk: true if the general-purpose AI model is classified as a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk under Article 51(1), because either (a) it has high-impact capabilities evaluated under Article 51(1)(a), with the Article 51(2) presumption applying where cumulative training computation is greater than 10^25 floating-point operations, or (b) the Commission has made the decision referred to in Article 51(1)(b), including designation under Article 52(4); false only where the evidence affirmatively establishes that neither Article 51(1) ground applies; null where that cannot be determined

art53.has_copyright_policy: true if the provider of the general-purpose AI model has put in place a policy to comply with Union law on copyright and related rights, in particular to identify and comply with, including through state-of-the-art technologies, a reservation of rights expressed pursuant to Art. 4(3) of Directive (EU) 2019/790 (Art. 53(1)(c)); false if it has not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art53.copyright_policy_evidence: List of free-text items: where the copyright policy and the methods used to identify and comply with reservations of rights expressed pursuant to Art. 4(3) of Directive (EU) 2019/790, including through state-of-the-art technologies, are documented. Empty list if there is nothing to report.
art53.has_training_data_summary: true if the provider has drawn up a sufficiently detailed summary about the content used for training the general-purpose AI model, according to the template provided by the AI Office (Art. 53(1)(d)); false if it has not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art53.training_data_summary_public: true if that summary has been made publicly available (Art. 53(1)(d)); false if it has not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art53.training_data_evidence: List of free-text items: where the training-content summary is documented or published. Empty list if there is nothing to report.
art53.is_open_source_gpai: true if the general-purpose AI model is released under a free and open-source licence that allows for the access, usage, modification and distribution of the model, and its parameters, including the weights, the information on the model architecture and the information on model usage, are made publicly available (Art. 53(2), Art. 54(6)); false if not; null if you cannot determine it from the project. Do not use the separate Art. 2(12) scope exclusion for AI systems to determine this GPAI-model exception.
art53.has_systemic_risk: true if the general-purpose AI model is a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk under Art. 51 (the open-source exceptions of Art. 53(2) and Art. 54(6) do not apply to such models); false if it is not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.

art54.is_open_source_gpai: true if the general-purpose AI model is released under a free and open-source licence that allows for the access, usage, modification and distribution of the model, and its parameters, including the weights, the information on the model architecture and the information on model usage, are made publicly available (Art. 54(6)); false if not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art54.has_systemic_risk: true if the general-purpose AI model is a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk under Art. 51 (the exception of Art. 54(6) does not apply to such models); false if it is not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art54.mandate_evidence: List of free-text items: where, before a general-purpose AI model is placed on the Union market, the written mandate by which a provider established in a third country appoints an authorised representative established in the Union is documented (Art. 54(1) to (3)). Empty list if there is nothing to report.

art55.has_incident_tracking: true if the provider of the general-purpose AI model with systemic risk keeps track of, documents and reports, without undue delay, to the AI Office and, as appropriate, to national competent authorities, relevant information about serious incidents and possible corrective measures (Art. 55(1)(c)); false if it does not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art55.incident_evidence: List of free-text items: where the process for keeping track of and documenting serious incidents, reporting relevant information about them without undue delay to the AI Office and, as appropriate, national competent authorities, and recording possible corrective measures to address them is documented. Empty list if there is nothing to report.
art55.has_cybersecurity_protection: true if the provider ensures an adequate level of cybersecurity protection for the general-purpose AI model with systemic risk and the physical infrastructure of the model (Art. 55(1)(d)); false if it does not; null if you cannot determine it from the project.
art55.cybersecurity_evidence: List of free-text items: where the cybersecurity protection of the general-purpose AI model with systemic risk and the physical infrastructure of the model is documented. Empty list if there is nothing to report.

art86.explanation_evidence: List of free-text items: where an affected person who is subject to a decision taken by the deployer on the basis of the output from a high-risk AI system listed in Annex III, other than a system listed under point 2 of Annex III, and where that decision produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects that person in a way that the person considers to have an adverse impact on their health, safety or fundamental rights, can obtain from the deployer clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system in the decision-making procedure and the main elements of the decision taken (Art. 86(1)), subject to Art. 86(2) and (3). Empty list if there is nothing to report.

art91.readiness_evidence: Free text: where the project documents how the provider of the general-purpose AI model, or its representative, supplies information requested by the Commission under Art. 91, including documentation drawn up under Arts. 53 and 55 or additional information necessary to assess compliance, within the period specified in the request. Leave empty if there is nothing to report.

art92.cooperation_evidence: Free text: where the project documents how, when the Commission requests access for an evaluation under Art. 92(1), the provider of the general-purpose AI model or its representative provides the requested access to the model within the period specified in the request, including through APIs or further appropriate technical means and tools, including source code where requested (Art. 92(3) to (5)). Leave empty if there is nothing to report.

art111.transition_evidence: Free text: evidence of the applicable compliance steps under Art. 111(1) and (2): for AI systems that are components of the Annex X large-scale IT systems and were placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2027, steps to bring them into compliance by 31 December 2030; for other high-risk AI systems placed on the market or put into service before the applicable Chapter III date, whether they are subject from that date to significant changes in design, with the applicable date being {chapter_iii_annex_iii} for systems classified under Art. 6(2) and Annex III and {chapter_iii_annex_i} for systems classified under Art. 6(1) and Annex I; and, in any case, for high-risk AI systems intended to be used by public authorities, steps by providers and deployers to comply by 2 August 2030. Leave empty if there is nothing to report.
art111.change_tracking_evidence: Free text: how changes to the design are tracked for a high-risk AI system, other than a system covered by Art. 111(1), that was placed on the market or put into service before its applicable Chapter III date, because Art. 111(2) makes the Regulation apply to such a system only if, from that applicable date, it is subject to significant changes in its design. The applicable date is {chapter_iii_annex_iii} for systems classified as high-risk under Art. 6(2) and Annex III, and {chapter_iii_annex_i} for systems classified as high-risk under Art. 6(1) and Annex I. This does not displace the separate requirement that providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems intended to be used by public authorities take the necessary steps to comply by 2 August 2030. Leave empty if there is nothing to report.
art111.gpai_timeline_evidence: Free text: what you found on the steps taken to comply with the Regulation by the date in Art. 111(3) for a general-purpose AI model placed on the market before the date set there. Leave empty if there is nothing to report.

art50.is_generating_synthetic_content: true if the AI system generates or substantially manipulates at least one in-scope synthetic audio, image, video or text output intended to be perceived, interpreted, verified or acted upon by natural persons for the purposes of Article 50(2). Apply the Commission's non-binding Guidelines C(2026) 5054, paragraph 68, as interpretative guidance. Do not count: short sequences such as single words, brief image captions, alt-text, UI labels or icon-scale graphics; source code in programming, scripting, markup, query or configuration languages intended to be interpreted, compiled or executed by software, including comments and contextual information integral to that code, and technical artefacts such as SDKs, SQL, infrastructure-as-code, YAML or JSON configuration, schemas, scripts, machine-readable specifications, APIs and software libraries; exclusively machine-to-machine outputs processed without human exposure; or non-final outputs used only in closed-loop production workflows. Do not automatically exclude substantive human-readable content merely because it is carried in JSON or markup, or because it relates to programming. Apply the Article 50(2) exceptions for assistive standard editing, no substantial alteration of the deployer's input or its semantics, and legally authorised criminal-law-enforcement uses where applicable. A coding assistant whose only output is excluded source code answers false; one that also produces substantive natural-language answers, standalone documentation, images or other in-scope human-facing content answers true. For true, name the in-scope output types and paths in marking_evidence. Answer false if the evidence establishes that there are no in-scope outputs; null if the available project evidence is insufficient to determine this. This field assesses output scope, not the identity of the legally responsible provider or the applicable compliance date.
art50.has_content_watermarking: true if at least one in-scope synthetic audio, image, video or text output type or path has an identifiable implementation intended to apply or associate a machine-readable mark indicating artificial generation or manipulation, such as embedded metadata, watermarking, a provenance signature or another technical marking mechanism. Detection does not have to be independently verified for this evidence flag to be true: true indicates an identified marking mechanism requiring human review, not compliance with Article 50(2). false if no such marking mechanism is identified for any in-scope synthetic output; null if the available project evidence is insufficient to determine whether a mechanism exists. Do not treat a standalone watermark configuration flag, declared metadata field or manifest format, or server log as proof that an output is actually marked. In marking_evidence, identify each mechanism and its code or configuration location where available; state which delivered output types and paths it covers, and how a person potentially exposed to the output can access a means of detection and obtain human-readable results (for example, an appropriate publicly available C2PA verifier, an accessible model-provider watermark detector, or an available provider or third-party detection service). If no detection means or access path was identified, say so explicitly. Also identify in-scope output types and paths for which marking or detectability is missing or cannot be verified. A mark, field, manifest, log or configuration flag alone does not establish detectability or Article 50(2) compliance.
art50.disclosure_evidence: List of free-text items identifying where natural persons are informed that they are interacting with an AI system for the purposes of Article 50(1), for example a notice displayed at or before the first interaction. Empty list if no such evidence is found.
art50.marking_evidence: List free-text items describing the marking and detection evidence, gaps and uncertainties for in-scope synthetic audio, image, video or text outputs under Article 50(2). For each relevant output type or path, identify the machine-readable marking mechanism, its code or configuration location where available, and the means by which a person potentially exposed to the delivered output can detect artificial generation or manipulation and obtain human-readable results. If no means of detection or access path was identified, state this explicitly rather than assuming that metadata, a C2PA manifest, a server log or a configuration flag proves detectability. Identify output paths that are unmarked or for which marking or detection cannot be verified, including where another path is marked. If an in-scope output is identified but no marking mechanism is found, record that negative finding; use an empty list only when there is no relevant evidence or identifiable in-scope output path to report.
art50.deep_fake_evidence: List of free-text items identifying where deployers disclose that image, audio or video content constituting a deep fake has been artificially generated or manipulated for the purposes of Article 50(4), first subparagraph. Empty list if no such evidence is found.
art50.public_interest_text_evidence: List of free-text items identifying either (i) where deployers disclose that AI-generated or manipulated text published for the purpose of informing the public on matters of public interest has been artificially generated or manipulated, or (ii) evidence that the exception in Article 50(4), second subparagraph, applies because the content has undergone human review or editorial control and a natural or legal person holds editorial responsibility for its publication. Empty list if no such evidence is found.
